entities.summary: Ansovinus, a bishop of Camerino, played a pivotal role in shaping the agricultural practices of the medieval European region. Born into an unknown year, Ansovinus rose to prominence as a religious leader, eventually being canonized as a saint. His legacy extended beyond his immediate community, influencing the development of farming techniques and promoting the value of agriculture as a vital component of medieval society. Ansovinus' feast day, celebrated on March 13, remains a testament to his enduring impact on the lives of those who revered him. The exact date of his death, on April 13, 861, serves as a poignant reminder of the transience of human life, even in the face of lasting cultural significance.
